name: Signed tool calls
summary: The agent signs each outbound request or action with a key tied to its identity, so the receiving service can verify who sent it and that it wasn't altered. Web Bot Auth does this for HTTP requests; AP2 does it for payment mandates.
how: Agent operator publishes a public key directory
Agent signs each request (e.g. HTTP Message Signatures, RFC 9421)
Receiver fetches the key and verifies the signature
Receiver applies its own policy to the verified identity
facts: IETF Web Bot Auth draft (Signature-Agent header, JWKS directory); AP2 signed mandates
Web Bot Auth is an IETF working-group draft (Sept 2026)
Verifiable identity, but says nothing about what the agent may do
goodFor: Agents that browse or call APIs at scale and want to be recognized
watchOut: Key management and rotation are on you
